clue.text: Fine with anything being contested

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ought is an old spelling of aught, meaning anything

explanation.surface: A fine imposed for anything at all is being disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: OUGHT here is the variant of aught, not the verb of obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fought over has been disputed in battle or argument, the past participle of fight.

clue.text: Rear took off, for example, skywards

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading skywards means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: fled means ran away, took off
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: A bird's back end took off into the sky, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a noun for the back; it is the verb to raise young.
explanation.definitionFit: To fledge a young bird is to rear it until it grows feathers and can fly.

clue.text: Axed from the off Ford left blunder in "The Horse Soldiers", say

indicators.note: something axed from the off is cut at the start, so the director's initial goes
left read as departed means the abbreviation for left goes too

blocks.note: a floater is a blunder or gaffe
the opening letter of Ford
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Director John Ford made a howler in his film The Horse Soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ford directed The Horse Soldiers (1959), a Western; both F and L leave the word for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An oater is slang for a Western film, named for horses' oats, and The Horse Soldiers is an example.

clue.text: Disfigured denarius not yet picked up

indicators.note: something disfigured is spoilt in shape, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the eight letters of this coin rearranged

explanation.surface: A damaged Roman coin lies on the ground, not yet collected.
explanation.walkthrough: A denarius was a Roman silver coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unraised means not lifted, so a coin still lying there has not been picked up.

clue.text: Object of expedition to regain most favourable plunder

blocks.note: golden means very favourable, as in a golden opportunity
to fleece is to rob or swindle

explanation.surface: An expedition sets out to win back its best loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Jason and the Argonauts sailed to Colchis to bring back the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Argonauts' voyage aimed to recover the ram's golden pelt for Jason's claim to the throne.

clue.text: Region's tense, I guess

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
'I bet' is a way of saying I suppose

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a certain area is tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a high plateau area of Asia, now an autonomous region of China.

clue.text: Picks holes in pinks

blocks.note: first meaning: finds fault with, criticises
second meaning: what a car engine does when fuel detonates early

explanation.walkthrough: Pinks looks like a colour or flowers; in motoring an engine that pinks is making a metallic rattle from premature ignition.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise is to run down, and an engine with early ignition rattles with the same verb as pinking.

clue.text: Massaged joint with advantage within day

indicators.note: within puts the advantage inside the joint

blocks.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
ad is tennis shorthand for advantage
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A sore joint was rubbed with good effect within a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work with the hands, pressing and squeezing as a masseur does.

clue.text: Picked up material for wrapping fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upward

blocks.note: Saran is a plastic cling film used for wrapping food

explanation.surface: Someone collects cling film to wrap up fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound-alike signal, but here it lifts the word upward in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The nara is a southern African shrub whose melon-like fruit is eaten, so naras are its fruits.

clue.text: Rebellious aspirant rendered plot poorly

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel claimant carried out his conspiracy badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Pretender was James Francis Edward Stuart, whose 1715 Jacobite rising failed.
explanation.definitionFit: James Stuart claimed the British throne and backed armed uprisings, an aspirant in rebellion.

clue.text: Predator loses strong lots mostly — one's busy with pram?

indicators.note: loses means lets go of, so the abbreviation is taken out of the bird
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the kestrel is a hawk that hunts small prey
str. is a dictionary abbreviation for strong
many means lots

explanation.surface: A predator that loses most of its strength ends up pushing a pram.
explanation.walkthrough: The pram is not a baby carriage but a flat-bottomed boat or lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelman worked the keels, flat barges on the Tyne, so he was kept busy with such boats.

clue.text: Reasonably canny about Scots article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cunning word goes round the Scots article

blocks.note: canny in the sense of shrewd or artful
ane is the Scots form of a or one

explanation.surface: A shrewd Scotsman writes something about his countrymen, quite sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanely means in a sound and sensible manner, so it acts as a synonym for reasonably.

clue.text: Fat clique quail when two Conservatives resign

indicators.note: Conservatives who resign leave office, so two of the letters standing for that party drop out

blocks.note: a clan is a close-knit group
the colin is an American quail, the bobwhite
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, taken twice

explanation.surface: A fat little group of birds cowers when two Tory ministers step down.
explanation.walkthrough: Both C's go: one from the front of CLAN, one from the front of COLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance from sheep's wool, a fat used in ointments and cosmetics.

clue.text: Trimmed tree near a Spanish village

indicators.note: trimming cuts something short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the alder is a waterside tree
the article a, placed next to the tree

explanation.surface: A pruned tree stands beside a little village in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' just puts A next to the shortened tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldea is the Spanish word for a hamlet or village, found in English dictionaries.

clue.text: Oilmen are here reversing demand on rogue that's down 50 per cent

indicators.note: something down by half has lost its second half, so only the first four of eight letters stay
reversing turns the following word round to read right to left
in a down-style build one thing placed on another follows it, so the demand goes second

blocks.note: aberrant means straying from the norm, as a rogue element does
a need is a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: Oil workers are said to be in a place where they keep backing away from an unruly demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the reversed demand after the halved rogue, as in a down-style build.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is the Scottish city that serves as the hub of the North Sea oil industry.

clue.text: Complete Papal See in shake-up? It's a disappointing thing

indicators.note: a shake-up rearranges things thoroughly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: dead means complete or utter, as in a dead loss
the eight letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A total upheaval at the Vatican would be a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dead Sea apple, or apple of Sodom, looked fair but turned to ashes when bitten.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary fruit looked lovely and crumbled to ash, so the phrase names anything that promises much and disappoints.

clue.text: Start of Great Fire that's troubled teen in times gone by

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone
something troubled is disturbed and stirred up, so its letters are mixed

blocks.note: the first letter of Great
the four letters of Fire rearranged

explanation.surface: The Great Fire of London troubled a teenager long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Teen is not an adolescent here: it is an archaic word for sorrow or injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic teen meant affliction or sorrow, a synonym for grief in older English.

clue.text: This helps fuel flight, ie journey taken in the past

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
tane is an old form of taken

explanation.surface: Fuel for a flight is described as a journey made long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Triptane is a hydrocarbon added to aviation fuel to raise its octane and stop knocking.

clue.text: Net being new unit of space

blocks.note: ens is a philosophical term for being or existence
N is the abbreviation for new
an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres

explanation.surface: A net is described as a fresh measure of empty area.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it, and to trap or snare it is the same action.

clue.text: About one flag (Nationalist) rising from coastal waters

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upward

blocks.note: C abbreviates circa, about
I is the Roman numeral one
to flag is to tire
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A nationalist flag is raised over the shoreline sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is the verb, to droop or grow weary, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Neritic describes the shallow sea over the continental shelf, so it belongs to coastal waters.

clue.text: Take French companies for short look-sees

blocks.note: rec. abbreviates recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions
Cie is the abbreviation for the French compagnie

explanation.surface: French firms are taken on brief inspection visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Reccies is informal for reconnaissances, quick exploratory visits.

clue.text: Old soil English put in pound

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, so the single letter goes within the larger word

blocks.note: to bray is to pound or crush, as in a mortar
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Old earth with an English element is placed in a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound is the verb, not money: bray in this sense means to crush small.
explanation.definitionFit: Beray is an obsolete verb meaning to befoul or defile, so 'old soil' as a verb fits.

clue.text: Just like Botham in past sending appearance money back

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the other way, so the word reads right to left
in places the payment inside the word meaning past

blocks.note: by means past, as in walking by
an appearance fee is paid to turn up

explanation.surface: Cricketer Ian Botham once returned his appearance fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham, the England cricket all-rounder, was nicknamed Beefy.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means brawny and burly, the build and the nickname of the cricketer.

clue.text: Stick with what's in satay's sweet ingredient?

indicators.note: only what lies inside the word is kept, so its outer letters are discarded

blocks.note: a bat is a stick for hitting a ball
the skewered meat dish, whose inner letters are wanted

explanation.surface: A skewer and the sweet part of satay sauce are put together.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the batata is the sweet potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Batata is another name for the sweet potato, a root used in dishes and desserts.

clue.text: I'd get in changes making an instance of selection

indicators.note: changes alter the order of things, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes changes to get onto the selected list.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing chooses what to keep and what to cut, so it is a process of selection.

clue.text: Old griffins run away from gross scene of battle

indicators.note: going away from a place means leaving it, so the run letter departs

blocks.note: gr. is the abbreviation for gross
Ypres in Belgium saw several First World War battles
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Mythical beasts flee a gruesome battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Grype is an obsolete word for a griffin or vulture, so grypes are griffins of old.

clue.text: Answer bishop in clipped style — to that extent, it's embroidery

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title abbreviated
as in as much as that

explanation.surface: A bishop gives a curt reply, and to that degree it is all fancy talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Clipped style is a bishop's form of address, Right Reverend, cut to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich tapestry wall hanging, loosely a piece of embroidered needlework.

clue.text: In Scotland plenty of bums on seats

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from letters across these words

blocks.note: the letters running across these words

explanation.surface: North of the border there are plenty of people in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Bums on seats is the showbiz phrase for paying audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonse is a Scots word for abundance or plenty.

clue.text: Sideways glance taking in priest who declared himself unclean?

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing something inside, so the glance holds the priest

blocks.note: a leer is a sly sidelong look

explanation.surface: A priest got a sideways look when he declared himself impure.
explanation.walkthrough: Leviticus required a person with leprosy to cry 'Unclean, unclean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Under biblical law someone with leprosy had to call out that they were ritually impure.

clue.text: Preposterous constant in father's reparations

blocks.note: a sire is a father
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.walkthrough: Preposterous comes from Latin prae (before) and posterus (after), hence its use as a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eric was the fine paid for a killing under old Irish law, a form of blood-money compensation.

clue.text: Possibly try courting round lane's end — drivers prefer to avoid it

possibly suggests one of many arrangements, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the last letter of lane

explanation.walkthrough: The drivers are golfers: tiger country is the deep rough off the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers hitting a driver off the tee want to stay clear of the heavy rough called tiger country.

clue.text: Beheaded martyr and saint of little fish

clue.text: Hired a Charlie who's no gent going west

clue.text: Energy behind scene's moving spirit

indicators.note: moving shifts things about, so the letters are rearranged

the letters of scene's, which energy sits beside

clue.text: Approach mark of femininity with acceptance having priority

the suffix -ess marks a female form, as in actress

clue.text: Right to go against leaving European assembly
